related_bodies.name: NASK AI Safety Research Centre
related_bodies.role: NASK's director describes "the cooperation between the Korea AI Safety Institute at ETRI and the AI Safety Research Center at NASK". On NASK's research teams page, the centre's Department of Security and Transparency of Artificial Intelligence says "We develop methods for generating, analyzing and auditing models, and develop methods and software to support their analysis". The Ministry of Digital Affairs quotes the centre's director: the centre "is also tasked with educating and supporting society in the informed use of modern AI technologies". NASK says the centre will lead its cooperation with OpenAI and "will research the safety of increasingly advanced AI systems" with it.

English searches for a national AI safety, security or evaluation institute, commitment, proposal or study. English searches found NASK's AI Safety Research Centre and the funded Eval FM research project on model safety evaluation. These are substantive safety research activities, but a national institute designation and severe-risk frontier-model mandate were not established. The existing AI Act law addresses regulatory supervision. Partial check only; the last full-check date is unchanged.

Retained none_identified at low confidence after reading Resolution 130, the ministry account and NASK's research-team description; updated the summary and related-body role. Partial check; the last full-check date is unchanged.
Selected the closest body against retrieved source text and excerpts; recorded its stage, evidence gap and limits. Partial check; the last full-check date is unchanged.

Changed status confidence from low to medium because the individual check has recorded English and national or official-language queries and retrieved primary governance evidence; classification disagreement no longer lowers confidence. Partial check; the last full-check date is unchanged.

Re-read Resolution 130 of the Council of Ministers of 9 June 2026 (Monitor Polski, 18 June 2026, position 620): it adopts the State Digitalisation Strategy and contains both passages on NASK's AI Safety Research Centre that the record quotes. The strategy names the AI policy of 2020 (Resolution 196 of 28 December 2020) as the one in force, with an update planned for 2026; no record text says an AI policy to 2030 was adopted. No change. Partial check, not a full record re-check.

News search from 17 October 2026 in English and Polish, with the digital affairs ministry's news page (newest 10 November). Added NASK's announcement of 23 October 2026 of its agreement with OpenAI on AI safety research, led on NASK's side by its AI Safety Research Centre, with OpenAI's description of the work from an archived copy, and CERT Polska's access to OpenAI cyber models from July 2026. No separate ministry announcement of the agreement, no new government act assigning national frontier evaluation, and no centre funding, staffing or centre-specific model-access terms were found. Partial check, not a full record re-check.

excerpts.text: Komisja Rozwoju i Bezpieczeństwa Sztucznej Inteligencji, zwana dalej „Komisją”, jest organem nadzoru rynku w zakresie systemów sztucznej inteligencji w rozumieniu art. 70 ust. 1 rozporządzenia 2024/1689.
excerpts.gloss: The Commission for the Development and Safety of Artificial Intelligence, hereinafter "the Commission", is the market surveillance authority for artificial intelligence systems within the meaning of Article 70(1) of Regulation 2024/1689.

excerpts.text: Komisja działa jako pojedynczy punkt kontaktowy, o którym mowa w art. 70 ust. 2 rozporządzenia 2024/1689.
excerpts.gloss: The Commission acts as the single point of contact referred to in Article 70(2) of Regulation 2024/1689.

excerpts.text: Minister właściwy do spraw informatyzacji jest organem notyfikującym, o którym mowa w rozdziale III sekcja 4 rozporządzenia 2024/1689.
excerpts.gloss: The minister responsible for digitalisation is the notifying authority referred to in Chapter III, Section 4 of Regulation 2024/1689.
